title: Fakeeh Medical KIT Integration (FHIR R4) - POST search
description:
# Fakeeh HIS ↔ Medical KIT integration API

HL7 FHIR R4 REST API used by the Medical KIT to **look up patients in Fakeeh HIS** and **record device readings**.

## Setup
1. Import this collection and the *Fakeeh Medical KIT – Local* environment, then select the environment.
2. Set `baseUrl` and `apiKey` for your target environment (the local values work against a developer machine).
3. Run **1. Patient lookup → Find patient by Iqama** first. It stores the patient id in `patientId`, which every reading request uses.

Patient data comes live from Fakeeh HIS. The FHIR `Patient.id` is the National ID / Iqama number, so readings reference `Patient/<national id>`.

## Conventions
- Every request except `GET /metadata` needs the header `X-Api-Key`. A missing or wrong key returns **401** with an `OperationOutcome`.
- Send and expect `application/fhir+json`.
- **All searches are POST (FHIR `_search`)**: `POST /Patient/_search` and `POST /Observation/_search`. Search parameters go in an `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` body, so no patient identifier (National ID / Iqama) appears in the URL or in server and proxy logs. Only `GET /metadata` and `GET /CodeSystem/...` stay GET because they carry no patient data.
- Every reading **must** carry a unique KIT reading id in `Observation.identifier` (system `http://fakeeh.example/medical-kit/reading-id`). Re-sending the same id is safe: the API returns **200** with the stored reading instead of creating a duplicate, so retries after a timeout are idempotent.
- `effectiveDateTime` **must** include a timezone offset, e.g. `2026-10-18T07:58:42+03:00`. Values without an offset are rejected with **400**.
- Units are UCUM (`valueQuantity.system = http://unitsofmeasure.org`). The accepted unit per field is listed by **Get vital types**.
- Errors are always returned as a FHIR `OperationOutcome`; `issue.diagnostics` has the human-readable reason.

## Sending readings
- **Recommended:** `POST /fhir` with a `batch` Bundle. Each entry is processed on its own, so one bad reading never blocks the others. The response is a `batch-response` with one entry per request entry, in the same order: `201` created, `200` already existed, `4xx` rejected (with an `OperationOutcome`).
- `POST /fhir/Observation` records a single reading.

## Vital type models
| Code | Shape |
|---|---|
| HR, TEMP, SPO2, WEIGHT, GLUCOSE | one Observation with `valueQuantity` |
| BP | one Observation with `component` systolic (LOINC 8480-6) and diastolic (LOINC 8462-4) |
| PF | one Observation with `component` `per_min` and `fev1_l` (both required) |
| BT, BC | **one Observation per field**; the field goes in `code.coding` with system `http://fakeeh.example/medical-kit/vital-field` |

Pre-request scripts set `2026-11-05T10:30:00+03:00` (current time, +03:00) and `MHL6Q2ZB` (unique per send) so the samples can be sent repeatedly. Replace them with real values in the KIT.

tags.name: 1. Patient lookup
tags.description: Wraps the Fakeeh HIS patient lookup. Search by National ID (starts with 1) or Iqama (starts with 2). A patient that does not exist returns **200** with an empty Bundle (`total: 0`), not 404.

tags.name: 3. Send readings – batch (recommended)
tags.description: Send readings as a FHIR `batch` Bundle to `POST /fhir`. Each entry succeeds or fails on its own. Check every `entry[i].response.status` in the reply.

tags.name: 4. Send readings – single Observation
tags.description: `POST /fhir/Observation` records one reading. The optional `If-None-Exist` header (or the `Observation.identifier`) is used to avoid duplicates.

tags.name: 5. Previous readings
tags.description: `GET /fhir/Observation` searches stored readings for one patient. `patient` is required. Results come in a `searchset` Bundle with `total` and `next`/`previous` links.

resource.documentation: Read-only proxy to Fakeeh HIS. Patient.id is the National ID / Iqama number. Search with POST [type]/_search and the parameters in an application/x-www-form-urlencoded body, so no patient identifier appears in a URL.

searchParam.name: _id
searchParam.documentation: Patient id (the National ID / Iqama number).

resource.documentation: Medical KIT device readings. Create is idempotent on the KIT reading id. Search with POST [type]/_search and the parameters in an application/x-www-form-urlencoded body, so no patient identifier appears in a URL.

searchParam.name: patient
searchParam.documentation: Patient/{id} from the Patient search. Required unless _id is given.

searchParam.name: _id
searchParam.documentation: Observation id, as returned by the create.

searchParam.name: code
searchParam.documentation: LOINC, vital-type or vital-field code, with or without system.

searchParam.name: date
searchParam.documentation: effectiveDateTime; repeatable; prefixes eq, ge, gt, le, lt.

searchParam.name: _page
searchParam.documentation: Opaque token from a self / previous / next link of a previous search.

resource.documentation: CodeSystem/medical-kit-vital-type lists the vital types and their fields.

operations.summary: Find a patient in Fakeeh HIS by National ID / Iqama.
operations.description: Wraps the Fakeeh HIS patient lookup. Search by National ID (starts with 1) or Iqama (starts with 2). A patient that does not exist returns **200** with an empty Bundle (`total: 0`), not 404.

requests.name: Find patient by Iqama
requests.description: POST-based FHIR search (`Patient/_search`). The identifier goes in the form body, not in the URL. Returns a `searchset` Bundle. The test script stores the patient id in `patientId`. The patient id is the National ID / Iqama number itself.

requests.name: Find patient by National ID
requests.description: Same as the Iqama search, for Saudi citizens (ID starts with 1). The identifier goes in the form body. Also stores `patientId`.

requests.name: Find patient – not found
requests.description: Unknown identifier → `200` with `total: 0`. Show "patient not found" in the KIT.

requests.name: Find patient by id (_id)
requests.description: FHIR has no POST read, so a patient is fetched by id with `_id` in the form body (the id is the National ID / Iqama, so it must not appear in the URL). Unknown id → `200` with `total: 0`.

operations.description: Send readings as a FHIR `batch` Bundle to `POST /fhir`. Each entry succeeds or fails on its own. Check every `entry[i].response.status` in the reply.

requests.name: Batch – all vital types
requests.description: One entry per vital type/field from *Vital Types.md*: BP, HR, SPO2, TEMP, WEIGHT, GLUCOSE, PF, BT (Hb, Na) and BC (BMI, visceral fat). All entries should return `201 Created`.

requests.name: Batch – duplicate reading (idempotent retry)
requests.description: The same reading id twice. The first entry is created (`201`), the second returns `200 OK` pointing to the stored reading. The KIT can safely resend a batch after a timeout.

requests.name: Batch – partial failure examples
requests.description:
Shows how rejected entries are reported while valid ones are still saved:
1. valid HR → `201`
2. `effectiveDateTime` without timezone → `400`
3. TEMP in °F (`[degF]`), only `Cel` is accepted → `400`
4. unknown vital type `XYZ` → `400`
5. PF missing the required `per_min` component → `400`

Each rejected entry carries an `OperationOutcome` in `entry[i].response.outcome`.

issue.diagnostics: Observation.effectiveDateTime must be a full date-time with a time zone, e.g. 2026-10-18T07:58:42+03:00.
Field 'Value' must use UCUM unit 'Cel', but '[degF]' was sent.

requests.name: Send Blood Pressure (BP)
requests.description:
Records one Blood Pressure (BP) reading. Returns **201 Created** with the stored Observation and a `Location` header. Re-sending the same reading identifier returns **200 OK** with the existing Observation (no duplicate is stored).

BP uses `component` for systolic and diastolic. `note` and the address extension are optional.

operations.description: `GET /fhir/Observation` searches stored readings for one patient. `patient` is required. Results come in a `searchset` Bundle with `total` and `next`/`previous` links.

requests.name: All readings for patient (newest first, paged)
requests.description: `_sort=-date` (default) or `date`. Page with `_count` and `_offset` in the body. Do not follow the `next` link if it is a GET URL: it would put the patient id in the URL. Ask the server to return an opaque `next` link or keep using `_offset`.

requests.name: Readings by vital type (local code)
requests.description: `code` accepts a vital type code (BP, HR, …) or `system|code`.

requests.name: Readings by category and date range
requests.description: `category` is `vital-signs` or `laboratory`. `date` supports `ge`, `gt`, `le`, `lt` prefixes and is sent twice (two form fields with the same name) for a range.

requests.name: Find one reading by id (_id)
requests.description: `observationId` is set by any of the single-Observation requests in folder 4. Fetched with `_id` in the form body (no POST read in FHIR).
